title: A nonspectrahedral hyperbolicity cone
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's counterexample (2026) to the geometric generalized Lax conjecture: the polynomial p(X,Z,y) = det((det X)Z - Phi_y(adj X)) of degree 20 in 23 variables, built from the Choi-Lam biquadratic form, is hyperbolic with respect to (I,I,0), and its hyperbolicity cone is not described by any linear matrix inequality of any size; the quotient p/det X of degree 16 has the same cone. Hyperbolic polynomials and Garding's convexity theorem with a complete proof; the Choi-Lam form is nonnegative but dominates no nonzero bilinear square; the positive map Phi_y, hyperbolicity of p and the slice Z >= Phi_y(X^-1); a hypothetical pencil is normalized to a Schur-complement inequality, rank-one limits give a norm identity, and its first variation produces a bilinear form whose square lies below the Choi-Lam form. OpenAI's companion theorem: the same cone is the projection of a spectrahedron of size 100 with 307 auxiliary variables. On each plane y = eta(cos t, sin t, 0) + xi(0, 0, 1) a Gram factorization of Q(y) gives a linear matrix inequality of size 20 for the slice; a moment functional on trigonometric polynomials with a degree-two matching identity replaces the angle.
prerequisites: linear algebra over R and C: determinants, adjugates, eigenvalues and orthogonal diagonalization of real symmetric matrices
derivatives of matrix-valued functions; Rouche's theorem from complex analysis

checks.reading: The manuscript 'A nonspectrahedral hyperbolicity cone' (OpenAI, 24 Sep 2026; build/main.tex and eight section files, about 40 kB of TeX; local library copy openai-math-20261006) was read in full on 17 Oct 2026, and every step was derived again while the lessons were written. No error was found. Changes of form in the course: (1) Garding's theorem, used for the degree-16 corollary, is proved in the course: hyperbolicity in every direction of the open cone through the roots of p(w + tau x + i alpha e) and Rouche's theorem, then convexity; (2) the facts on real symmetric matrices are collected and proved (the spectral theorem by the Rayleigh quotient, square roots, the Schur complement, kernels of sums, continuity of the largest eigenvalue); (3) the principal-minor criterion for positive semidefiniteness is proved through the characteristic polynomial; (4) added: the Choi-Lam form is not a sum of squares of bilinear forms (Corollary 2.4), Phi_y is not a sum of congruences linear in y (Exercise 3.2), and the role of v_0 != 0 in the last step (Exercise 4.1); (5) the appendix of OpenAI's text, a one-variable path contradicting an intermediate assertion in a preprint of Gonzalez Nevado, is not reproduced. Field state on 17 Oct 2026: Kummer and Netzer (arXiv:2609.24542, 21 Sep 2026) prove the conjecture for strictly hyperbolic polynomials; p is not strictly hyperbolic. The second manuscript of the family treated here, 'An exact semidefinite lift of a nonspectrahedral hyperbolicity cone' (OpenAI, 5 Oct 2026; main.tex and five section files, about 30 kB of TeX), was read in full on 17 Oct 2026, and every step was derived again; no error found. Changes of form: the polarized Gram identity is stated separately; the frequencies in the matching lemma are derived explicitly; the matrices of the lift are named G_j to keep B_j = B(r_j); exercises add the case S = 0 and the point (0, I, k), whose characteristic polynomial t^13 (t-1)(t-2)(t+1)(t^2-t-1)^2 has negative roots.

open_obligations: The OpenAI repository has a Lean entry for this family (lean/docs/095.md); it and the Lean files were not read, and the course does not depend on them.
The family's manuscript on hyperbolicity cones without semidefinite lifts (98 kB), which disproves the projected form of the conjecture, is not treated in this course.
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
